summary.headline: Indigo Paints Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18.7% to INR350 crore with EBITDA margin up to 17.7%, its best Q1 margin in four years.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew 18.7% YoY to INR350 crore, with double-digit volume and value growth across all four product categories. EBITDA rose 42% to INR61.9 crore (margin 17.7% vs 14.8%), and PAT rose 60.7% to INR42.4 crore, helped partly by a mark-to-market treasury gain. Consolidated revenue was INR369.7 crore (+19.7%), but subsidiary Apple Chemie's margins were compressed by high-cost inventory and limited B2B pass-through. Management said it will spend more aggressively on trade and influencers in Q2 to widen the growth gap versus the industry, and that the Jodhpur capex cycle is complete.

financial_highlights.change: +60.7% YoY (vs INR26.4 crore; margin 8.8%); includes MTM treasury gain

segments.name: Primers and distempers
segments.commentary: Value growth almost 30% and volume growth above 18%, the fastest-growing category in the quarter.

segments.name: Putty and cement paints
segments.commentary: Value growth above 21% and volume growth close to 14%.

segments.name: Enamel and wood coatings
segments.commentary: Value growth 17.5% and volume growth close to 10%.

segments.name: Emulsions (largest category)
segments.commentary: Value growth above 17% and volume growth around 12.5%.

segments.name: Apple Chemie (subsidiary, B2B)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR19.7 crore (+40%+) but profitability compressed by high-cost inventory and inability to pass through input costs; management expects gross margin recovery through Q2 and normal levels by Q3. Company proposes to acquire a further 11% stake, taking holding to 62%.

guidance_outlook: Q2 spends on trade and influencer engagement to rise further to widen the gap between Indigo's top-line growth and the industry; management noted bottom line grew faster than top line, meaning it 'did not do enough'.
No concrete Q2 margin guidance; management called the raw material situation a 'fuzzy' roller coaster and said Q2 is seasonally the weakest margin quarter, suggesting a six-month comparison.
July was a very good month with top-line momentum maintained or slightly better than Q1; August not yet assessed.
No new price increases planned as of now; a price cut in H2 is possible, most likely post-Diwali, with trade spends reduced correspondingly.
Growth versus industry is not formally guided; management said the gap could be about 10 percentage points if industry growth is around 15%, and it would not give a concrete number.
No significant capex expected for the next three years after the Jodhpur water-based plant.
EBITDA margin could decline about 1 percentage point or rise 0.5 percentage point in the coming period; management said margin is not the focus.
A/P spends are to be assessed on an annual basis; brand investment for the full year is 'undiminished'.
capex_capacity: Jodhpur water-based plant: 90,000 kilolitres per annum, in final commissioning; trial production expected within about 10 days of the call, per management, and to stabilise in about a month. Delay was attributed to a slow civil contractor, not raw material issues.
Solvent-based Jodhpur plant already in production for several months and ramping up.
Legacy water-based plant to be scrapped and output shifted to the new automated plant; opex expected to be broadly unchanged.
Solar capacity installed 350 kW across Pune and Cochin; a further 1,200 kW planned at Jodhpur.
No significant capex planned for the next three years; free cash flow expected to improve versus the last five years.
demand_pricing: Industry demand has improved progressively from Q3 FY26; management said demand is back near normal growth conditions.
Price increases in March and April were steep and frequent, protecting margins; raw material costs have eased from peaks but remain elevated and volatile.
Channel overstocking not seen at Indigo; management said the market leader may have seen some overstocking.
Distribution: about 19,400 active dealers (up about 800 YoY) and about 12,400 active tinting machines (up about 1,100 YoY).
Wood coatings: two-pack polyurethane launch planned for September and October in phases, in a segment management estimates at upwards of INR9,000 crore; it had no presence there earlier.
Differentiated products are about 29% to 30% of revenue; management said the company is not planning new differentiated launches.
Competition: management said no meaningful change from JSW's acquisition of AkzoNobel or the Birla Opus entry.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Indigo not grown faster versus the market leader, and was the IPL advertising pause a missed opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said steep, frequent price hikes benefit the market leader most. The IPL pause was due to raw material uncertainty after the Iran war, not competitor ad intensity or Dhoni's playing status; it intends to put the money back in the coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is July and August demand holding after Q1 upstocking, and is there a destocking risk for Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel overstocking was not seen at Indigo. July was a very good month with momentum maintained or slightly better than Q1; August was too early to call.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a price cut in H2, and what are the Q2 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No further price hikes are planned for now. A price cut is possible, most likely after Diwali. No Q2 margin guidance was given; management suggested looking at the six-month period.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jodhpur plant opex impact, and what is the competitive intensity after JSW-AkzoNobel?
qa_highlights.answer: The new plant replaces the legacy water-based plant with little opex change. Competitive intensity is unchanged, as JSW and AkzoNobel still operate separately.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new plant be ready for the festive season, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production is about 10 days away and should stabilise in about a month. The legacy plant is a backup. Management said gross margin may drop a couple of points, and EBITDA margin may move about 1 point either way.

risks_watch: Raw material prices remain elevated and volatile after the Iran war disruption; Q2 margin path is uncertain given mixed inventory costs.
Festive-season execution depends on the Jodhpur water-based plant stabilising in about one month after trial production.
Apple Chemie margin recovery depends on consuming high-cost inventory by Q2 and normal margins by Q3.
Management plans to spend more on trade and influencers in Q2, which may pressure gross margin by a couple of percentage points.
Possible H2 price cuts post-Diwali if input costs stay at current levels.
Wood coatings two-pack PU launch in September and October is a new category push that needs a specialised sales team.
Quarter's PAT margin includes a mark-to-market treasury gain, so underlying profit growth may be lower than reported.
key_quotes: Revenue has grown in double digits, the first such quarter in almost two years for us.
The fact that the bottom line grew faster than the top line very clearly means that we did not do enough.

I will not give any guidance for what the margin situation is going to be in Q2 because we have gone through a pretty much of a roller coaster ride as far as both the raw material input prices are concerned and our selling prices.
So it is very hard to give a very concrete number guidance on that, except that there should be a substantial gap between our top line growth and the rest of the industry.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand recovery, volume breadth and the completed capex cycle, with management stating it is "distinctively stronger" entering FY27. Cautious and evasive on forward margins: it declined to give Q2 margin guidance, called raw material costs a "fuzzy" roller coaster, and would not put a number on growth versus industry.
